critical.issue: If cv.skills is stored as a list of dicts (e.g. [{name,level}]), server.py:2637 (modern) and server.py:2850 (classique) crash with TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, dict found → 500. The frontend currently stores skills as strings, but there is NO Pydantic validation on PUT /api/cv (accepts raw dict), so any API consumer (or a future frontend refactor) can wedge PDF export. Defensive fix: coerce each skill via `(s if isinstance(s,str) else s.get('name',str(s)))`.

minor.issue: Endpoint shape is undocumented in tests — frontend uses /api/applications (no /mine suffix); confirm naming consistency across docs.

ui_bugs.issue: <input type='date'> shows browser default 'mm/dd/yyyy' (US format) instead of fr-FR or shadcn Calendar — bad UX for French users.

issues: React hydration warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option> — likely the Emergent dev overlay injecting x-excluded spans, but visible in console as error. Native <select>/<option> avoids shadcn Select overlay issues so functionally OK.

PUT /api/cv accepts a raw dict without Pydantic — same pattern flagged previously for /api/profile-v2. While the route uses allowed_fields whitelist (good), there is no per-field type validation. A client can PUT {skills:[1,2,3]} or {educations:'foo'} and break downstream code.

rca of the issue: build_cv_pdf modern (server.py:2637) and classique (server.py:2850) call `' · '.join(cv['skills'])` which requires every skill to already be a string. The frontend CVPage stores skills as plain strings (canonical format), but the backend never enforces this via Pydantic — so anyone PUTting {skills: [{name:'Python'}]} (which my initial test did, mirroring the future feature where skills get a level) crashes both PDF templates with TypeError. Fix: replace each occurrence with `' · '.join(s if isinstance(s,str) else s.get('name','') for s in cv['skills'])`. Reproduce: PUT /api/cv with skills=[{'name':'Python'}], then GET /api/cv/export?template=modern → 500.
